title: What fractions give the lengths of these two blue lines?
description: A number line has each unit cut into five equal parts, with two blue lines starting at zero. The board finds the size of one part and counts the parts under each blue line, then checks both against the labelled mark. Keeko doubts the shorter line by counting the mark at zero.
teaching_notes: One idea: each line is its count of equal parts times one part, here one fifth. Watch for students who count marks instead of parts and read a labelled mark as the end of a line.

source: On a number line from 0 to 2, each unit is divided into 5 eq
video_script.why: A learner reads two lengths on one number line by counting equal parts for each line.
video_script.substitution: the book's own number line with each unit cut into five equal parts
video_script.anchor: the number line from 0 to 2 with each unit cut into five equal parts and two blue lines from 0
video_script.wrong_answer: the shorter line is three fifths, because it touches three marks
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts the mark at zero as well, so the shorter line seems to touch three marks and to be three parts long.
video_script.payoff_line: The blue lines are two fifths and four fifths of a unit long
video_script.fraction_reading: one fifth, two fifths, three fifths, four fifths
never_show: 3/5 as the length of the shorter line
maths_rules: 1 unit cut into 5 equal parts: each part is 1/5 unit
shorter line ends at the 2nd mark: 2 x 1/5 = 2/5
longer line ends at the 4th mark: 4 x 1/5 = 4/5
check: the labelled mark 3/5 is the 3rd mark, between the 2nd and the 4th
video_script.design: One number line with five parts in each unit and two blue lines from zero. The labelled marks one fifth and three fifths stay on screen as a check.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a number line from 0 to 2; each unit cut into five equal parts; marks 1/5 and 3/5 labelled; two blue lines from 0, one to the second mark and one to the fourth mark

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.line: the number line appears with each unit cut into five equal parts and two labelled marks
marks.blue: two blue lines run from 0, one to the second mark and one to the fourth mark

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it uses a number line.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Each unit is cut into five equal parts. Two marks are labelled, one fifth and three fifths.
<bookmark mark='blue'/>Two blue lines start at zero. One ends at the second mark, and one ends at the fourth mark.
Which fractions give the lengths of the blue lines?

beats.on_screen: the number line and the blue lines stay; the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the five parts of the first unit in five shades; the labelled marks lit; the unlabelled marks drawn plain

marks.parts: the five parts of the first unit get five shades
marks.labels: the two labelled marks light up
marks.plain: the marks between them are drawn plain, with no label

beats.colours: five shades for the five parts
narration: <bookmark mark='parts'/>Each of the five equal parts of a unit is one fifth.
<bookmark mark='labels'/>The labels show the first mark and the third mark.
<bookmark mark='plain'/>The marks between them have no label, so we must work them out.

beats.on_screen: Given: each unit is cut into 5 equal parts; the blue lines end at the 2nd mark and the 4th mark
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, each unit is cut into five equal parts. The blue lines end at the second and fourth marks.

beats.on_screen: To find: the fractions for the lengths of the two blue lines
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the fractions that give the lengths of the two blue lines.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 1 unit into 5 equal parts, each part = 1/5

marks.size: one part is lit and labelled 1/5

narration: <bookmark mark='size'/>Step one, find the size of each part. One unit cut into five equal parts gives one fifth each.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: shorter line covers 2 parts, so 2 x 1/5

marks.short: the shorter blue line is traced and two parts are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='short'/>Step two, the shorter line ends at the second mark. It covers two parts, so we multiply two by one fifth.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: longer line covers 4 parts, so 4 x 1/5

marks.long: the longer blue line is traced and four parts are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='long'/>Step three, the longer line ends at the fourth mark. It covers four parts, so we multiply four by one fifth.

beats.on_screen: Check: the labelled mark 3/5 lies between the two ends: 2 parts, 3 parts, 4 parts

marks.check: the labelled mark lights up between the two line ends
marks.sides: one part is shaded on each side of the labelled mark

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, the labelled third mark must sit between the two ends. <bookmark mark='sides'/>The shorter line stops one part before it, and the longer line goes one part past it.

beats.on_screen: Answer: shorter line = 2/5 unit, longer line = 4/5 unit
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The blue lines are two fifths and four fifths of a unit long.
The shorter line is two fifths, and the longer line is four fifths.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says the shorter line is 3/5 because it touches 3 marks; the labelled mark 3/5 lights up one part past the end of the shorter line; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: the bubble with the wrong idea appears
marks.past: the labelled third mark lights up one part past the end of the shorter line
marks.fix: the mark at 0 is crossed out and the two parts light up

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the shorter line is three fifths, because it touches three marks.
<bookmark mark='past'/>But the label three fifths sits one part past the end of the shorter line.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Zero is only where we start. We count the parts a line covers, and that is two.
